notes.title: Devlog #4: The Lost Hotel
notes.notes:
[p]What does a spaceship hotel need apart from a reception and rooms for the hotel guests? Yup, a crew to steer and control the spaceship![/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44187377/4926e16d08d19f7f16e65164fec8a4b6f15d496e.png"][/img][/p][p]On the 5th floor of the hotel there are crew quarters, a canteen and of course the bridge. The rooms are still under construction, but the new characters have just been finalised.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44187377/ebc51464184cbd5dcaa7f0a55138ac55f17fa4bb.png"][/img]
The crew consists of 8 crew members and they can only rarely be encountered at the start of the game, as you as the player do not yet have access to certain rooms. However, when you meet the individual characters and get to know them, you realise that there is a little soap opera of its own going on on the 5th floor with all kinds of drama. I don't want to give any more away at this point, just this much: you will have an influence on it.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44187377/c624dd9b89840b761f82db1c72ef324921e978fe.png"][/img][/p][p]May I now introduce (from left to right):[/p][list][*][p]Undine "Dini" - Security Cadet[/p][/*][*][p]Bram - Chief of Security and Chef[/p][/*][*][p]T.J. - first officer[/p][/*][*][p]Captain Carter[/p][/*][*][p]San'dar "Sandy" - Navigator[/p][/*][*][p]Faelanduin "Fael" - Analytics and Xeno Specialist[/p][/*][*][p]Riven - Analytics Cadet[/p][/*][*][p]Novaleen "Nova" - Mechanic and Technician[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44187377/037ecf0e81784f3ad659e0a84fcb71477477fcf1.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]Here's a little behind-the-scenes look at how I developed the characters' profile pictures. First I created the character, then I tried out different poses and pixelated the one I was most happy with into a profile picture. A profile picture consists of about 8-10 layers, with the bottom layer simply being the black outlines and flat filled colour. Everything else I call "render" and provides the necessary depth, consisting of light and shadow layers, colour accents and coloured contours.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44187377/a86a6004fcecf2ba9210938e75c62f307fe4608a.png"][/img][/p][p]Each NPC will of course have different facial expressions, ranging from neutral to cheerful to angry, which will be visible during dialogues. If you want to know more about the dialogue system, have a look at my Devlog #3![/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44187377/e117b6229649228f587cd54a126e3c2f58c88c18.png"][/img][/p][p]I've also been working on a new UI style. First of all, there's an Octowheel to select certain areas such as items, a map or an overview of all NPCs.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44187377/07154b00c78234e37e88d959917a85128f8432a5.gif"][/img][/p][p]For the Octowheel, I've already received a lot of positive feedback on Reddit, as well as a few tips for improving, and I couldn't be more grateful for it.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44187377/1c24e5aba7a00068da70d1687d2c4f66ec4f3e90.png"][/img][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44187377/55102d05e17020790a48cc5391f10f779ba5e2db.png"][/img][/p][p]There's still a lot to do on the UI, because so far I've only finished the area for items and for the NPCs.[/p][p]
That's it for today :D

Best regards,
pixlerin[/p]

notes.title: Devlog #3: The Lost Hotel
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44187377/1c3ac80d0533b57d5c6a8401855d358b9f7430ea.gif[/img]

An important gameplay mechanic is the dialogue system, which I want to make feel dynamic and natural. This means that when you talk to a character for the first time, you really have to pay attention, because you can't repeat the dialogue right after you finish it, and the character might get annoyed with you the more you try to talk to them.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44187377/7128023468bf3ac2e17d9c341f043d11d3a76a88.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44187377/dbeef4e30af592b63241aa1f55769a468f29a7c7.png[/img]

No worries, the timeloop will save your socialising skills! You can repeat the dialogue every day, as the NPCs will forget what happened before and unlock more answer options to steer conversations in certain directions. There will also be a log in your device, also known as the player menu, where you can re-read the conversation and remember any forgotten information.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44187377/04e927cd7eb051d558f162ac6275c37158d7bd82.png[/img]

As you talk to different characters or find out information about them through the ongoing story, more options will be unlocked.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44187377/93ed80907e851936680db02b7bc4865ca749dabd.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44187377/1ecbaf781c1a0c3485226ea49f4790d29adef1fd.png[/img]

Don't worry about seeming like a weirdo who knows everything about a person and shocks them with all their information. I came up with the idea of memory fragments that can be unlocked at certain key events with the characters. So if you trigger a memory or a feeling in them by asking them certain questions, or telling them something profound, or even giving them a gift, they will remember you and that conversation throughout the time loop. This way, you as the player don't feel like an outsider because you're always the new face, and everyone else isn't seeing you for the first time. This could lead to some déja-vus, controversy and confusion.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44187377/5c7356a2f2ffc4878fda0ca2a7dcb255cb95269b.png[/img]

As you build deeper relationships with characters by collecting memory fragments and increasing the level of friendship or even romance options, you'll be able to visit them in their rooms (which you can also hack into as a hotelier, but that's another story) and unlock more tasks, information and items that you'll need to continue the story. I also want to make some things optional so that you don't feel the pressure to date every single character and just play as you like.

So that was the premise for the dialogue system. Let's take a look at the technical implementation of this logic!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44187377/754839a7749f363a0b63752ba2421046f0c49a1b.png[/img]

First, I started writing the dialogues in a spreadsheet before even thinking about the final structure. For some of the dialogues, which are shorter and easier to keep track of, a graphical solution would have been best. For more complicated conversations and different entry points, the graphs would have exploded and made it difficult to follow all the arrows.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44187377/d37bf31765ff02784fa4643e78226b3082cda487.png[/img]

There are ways of structuring data in software and one of them is JSON. In GDScript I can read a JSON file and translate it into a dialogue dictionary that makes the dialogues in the game accessible.

A dialogue always consists of one or more dialogue nodes containing the dialogue text. These nodes follow each other to create an RPG-like dialogue that you can continue by pressing a button. To know which node follows another, each node needs an individual key and a next key to know which one comes next. Here is a quick example of the spreadsheet snippet above:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44187377/fba03525a728529b46423043e868333117117c0f.png[/img]

Then I added the dialogue options. Each option also has a next key to define which node comes after the player chooses a particular option, of course it also has a text and a flag to define if the option is unlockable.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44187377/105836526caba365a429ec5da0413a2e1f8c38f1.png[/img]

To make the whole conversation more immersive, I added emotions to the nodes to change the portrait image of the character we are talking to.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44187377/c54329dc724be288fb4de766cca83a3f9d075210.png[/img]

In addition, the nodes have some things they unlock when a certain dialogue node is reached. For example, one dialogue unlocks an item that the player collects right after the text is displayed. Another dialogue option increases the level of friendship with the character.

This node unlocks a memory fragment:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44187377/76b179ef833f3b7c09c5fa7ee6dfb83c0dd989e0.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44187377/0a221394f059a9e3ce2b857034d096fb68450aa2.png[/img]

With the memory fragment, the player can trigger a completely new dialogue with new nodes and options the next day when the time loop is reset.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44187377/ad277dae9355d9158cf017bd68ded522707cc641.gif[/img]

EDIT: I almost forgot to mention it. At the moment we (my partner and I) are trying to visualise the dialogues with a graph generator to make it easier to spot mistakes and track the dialogues in a similar way to Detroit: Become Human.
At the moment, the generated graph looks like this (it's a snippet and intentional that you can't read the text):

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44187377/47ac6ccad00c11e77be08712182685edc66a99ff.png[/img]

That's it for today :D

Best regards,
pixlerin

notes.title: Devlog #2: The Lost Hotel
notes.notes:
Before I bring you up to date on the dialogue system, I would like to briefly inform you that there will be some mechanisms in the game that can be described as mini-games.
The Lost Hotel will have a number of features and mini-games that should be a nice way to pass the time, but are also good for unlocking areas or dialogue options.

I dedicated the whole two months of September and October to the development of three mini-games called "Cocktail Mixer", "Code Hacker" and "CapsulePets" (that they all start with a C might be a coincidence).
One of them has even been released, please read to the end to find out which one and where :D

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44187377/4b5ff88f8638c6e5f7136e0d59c33d53bf67ddae.png[/img]

One of the first things you can do in the game is to create your own hotelier signature drink at the lobby bar. You decide the shape of the glass, the ingredients by taste, aroma and texture, as well as a range of different toppings. There are endless ways to mix a customised cocktail, and once you've found more ingredients, there's even more. When you're done, you can name your cocktail and if the hotel guests are curious enough to try it, they'll order it. You can mix everything from completely neutral water to the creamiest sour-bitter-earthy drinks.
Later in the game, you can mix drinks for some of the guests according to their personal preferences.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44187377/f27c2075c351b60dd7d5fe1268783fd3a01114b9.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44187377/bf33c93a78d3162971885527b2c9759159dee7b9.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44187377/07affd261d0f45a60967ecb382607a6e5deff41c.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44187377/ff04739ab3fbfc3ae396fc4353b32fd99fc3ad80.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44187377/d1085418d022fadb4e54d0e72860376269e845cd.png[/img]

A somewhat simpler game than Cocktail Mixer is Code Hacker. You gain access to some hotel rooms by 1. having the corresponding level in electronics and 2. guessing the room code with the code hacking function. The higher your level, the more difficult the codes you can crack. I'm thinking about limiting the guessing to a certain number of attempts or adding more letters or symbols, but this is the current state for now.
The game is inspired by MasterMind and Wordle, just in case you were wondering :)

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44187377/d4bf92cbaf9a9ec79f1730428ac0ab7f8e175d20.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44187377/cac4aada3a343ab13ead93ab5ce320c9872f440d.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44187377/545a0ef6ad2b30316725cee1a57b4f87a371c0e0.png[/img]

The third mini-game can only be played inside the arcade room. So I designed that first.
At the beginning, the room is locked and only serves as a storage room. Your task is to gain access and breathe life into the room. Maybe you can repair the machines or find a few hidden ... items?!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44187377/140e5d2c6e1276727dc589b506903b5f0ee1e183.png[/img]

One of the three slot machines is not broken. The game that can be played on said machine is called CapsulePets, and being a 90s kid who grew up with Pokémon and still plays Pokémon games, it's heavily inspired by Pokémon battles. You can battle and collect pets to earn points and level up on the leaderboard.
There are 4 elements - fire, water, earth and air - and for each element there are 4 pets. So in total I have created 16 pets to collect.
For each element there is an epic pet that is stronger and rarer than the other 3.
Each captured pet gives points, the stronger the more points.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44187377/cbd2b62c6d96feada7bd6621c089a9e9429e2430.png[/img]

I published the game on Itch.io, so if you want to check it out, go ahead! The leaderboard is already quite full!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44187377/f90c55d2d9fa427848588d31291b0cf35d96d050.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44187377/9116be934817cba4feac0ee24c0ae7ff1d95fc07.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44187377/2a2ff40366964a3cc223a037f95f44b4ee37cf6e.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44187377/241559ffff84f41d6447aece19068192ab9f2bd7.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44187377/65d5bc4359cd09a19eb3585e2970349d1a38c639.png[/img]

That's it for today :D

Best regards,
pixlerin

notes.title: Devlog #1: The Lost Hotel
notes.notes:
It's about time for another update! Of course, I'm still working passionately on my game so that I can release a small demo this year. But I don't want to promise anything, I want to do it right and not quick & dirty.

In case you haven't noticed: the shop page now has new images and a brand-new cinematic teaser.

I've been focusing a lot on the characters over the last few months, both in terms of designing and writing the story and dialogue.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44187377/fa8ff4de29a67ed95f908f7bb8222d6832bb08bc.png[/img]

As with other games, you start out as a bored employee - in this case in the hotel industry - dreaming of a better life, when suddenly a job offer appears on the screen: "Hotelier Wanted".
"Why not?", you think, and apply immediately.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44187377/3b1bb9521d93e48844527782d3bd44643c51054d.png[/img]

It's not long before a shuttle arrives to pick you up. A shuttle? Yes, and it will take you for 4 days through space to a hotel spaceship, the Lodestar Hotel.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44187377/6f5845afd32cfe3d5e4533bb94aab612ce7e00c1.png[/img]

There you are greeted by an unusual pair of twins called Paige and Paige, both androids and receptionists at the Lodestar Hotel. They explain your new duties as the hotelier and soon send you to bed.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44187377/0afa088ce829621050655de622cbdf5f01b50fa2.png[/img]

The next day gets off to a turbulent start. Robots try to clean your room and kick you out, there's an explosion in the kitchen with casualties, guests complain about the poor state of the rooms and argue with each other. It feels like everything is going wrong. How do you cope?

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44187377/055f4249a3ad4cbbfcc99a0636ae210b05183cf4.png[/img]

You try to familiarise yourself with the technology and the administration, offer to help the guests, look after the equipment in the infirmary and then go to bed exhausted in the evening, hoping to take care of the rest tomorrow.
But when you wake up, nothing is the same as the night before. Everything starts all over again: the robots, the explosion, the unhappy guests,... It's as if yesterday never happened.
And the next day is like your first day at work again.
And the next.
And the next.
What's going on here? The Paiges can't help you, the guests don't seem to know anything. You seem to be the only person in the hotel who knows. So you try to figure out how to escape this time loop. You use the knowledge you have gained to extract information from the guests and staff and try to acquire more and more skills.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44187377/014397242dccbebc0cbad2cb4a3f008e3c1a8c99.png[/img]

Suddenly, strange things start to happen. People, silhouettes and sounds appear to you. Guests remember conversations they had with you. Some of your actions don't undo themselves overnight. The hotel seems to have some sort of memory. Can you use this to your advantage? Can you manipulate your guests and staff to get more information? Can you save yourself and the hotel and escape this madness?

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44187377/e5b71ab5d9e23188ac45c4f752f295e180d54e38.png[/img]

I've already introduced you to the NPCs, but there was still a lot missing to breathe life into them. These include walking and idle animations, the portraits and the dialogues. I've already finished a few things, but there's still a lot to do.

First few NPCs:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44187377/132743569a58c1858887c1f6e72123ce1d434341.png[/img]

Each character has their backstory, character arc, daily routines, relationships, purpose, dialogues with different choices, etc.
The more you learn about the characters, the more additional information you can squeeze out of them. Key events unlock memory fragments so that the NPCs remember certain conversations and you again after resetting the time loop. This allows you to change the course of the day and prevent or trigger certain events.
The first dialogues are already finished and resemble a heavily branched tree :D There is so much to plan! And I love it!!! In the next update I will talk more about the dialogue system.

I hope you'll stay tuned and thank you for all the support and feedback I've received on the various platforms. I look forward to further progress and the next updates :)

Best regards,
pixlerin

notes.title: Devlog #0: The Lost Hotel
notes.notes:
Hello, pixlerin here! I thought it was time for an update.
I'm working on [b]The Lost Hotel[/b] alongside my normal job as a software developer. It's my big dream to release this game one day and my motivation is huge ːsteamhappyː

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44187377/e8efabcf6e9a4dc601a330a886cbcbd21b5c5eab.png[/img]
Once I had the idea for The Lost Hotel in my head, I was immediately hooked. I started designing the characters and the lobby of the hotel, as the graphics of the game play an important role for me and the nostalgic effect.
This is what the lobby looked like at the beginning:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44187377/fd72d9b73b3fde9a711cb0210da1b03d5d5a28c9.png[/img]

But since the hotel is in space and is supposed to be a kind of spaceship/space station, I thought it was too unfuturistic. I tried to combine the classic hotel look with science fiction and ended up here:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44187377/7bcd9ef452ac5d01d6c9aadc37779e21f503a450.png[/img]

But this is far from the final product :D I've still got a few things to work on and already have a new sketch for the lobby on my computer, which will be realised soon.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44187377/d4df1cfc8e9fda32bfdf4bf5403d91d946405c26.png[/img]

The characters haven't changed since the beginning because I'm fully behind them and love them very much :D They've been so firmly anchored in my head for so long that they're like family to me haha, sounds crazy.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44187377/2b8947081c3a9f004af4982ea2cbbdcd00bc53db.png[/img]

I also designed the hoteliers and gave each one a personality and a special key.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44187377/1b2c113e1ac8ec99ca735df5932a7657409eb8bd.png[/img]

When I had completed the first version of the lobby, including the bar area and entrance, I ventured into a new room: the shuttle that picks the player up at the very beginning of the game. There they can familiarise themselves with the game's controls and personalise their character.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44187377/c18c66d64a76c98e2c6f80d1c016a6370f83d009.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44187377/3cce17295ce30e17f255cf5c4d55f4432bb9b121.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44187377/70eb6ded1b0a86d1178f17e7368ab175cfcc1e30.png[/img]

After the shuttle, I continued with the player's hotel room. I did a lot of research and tried out several versions of the floor plan until I ended up with the final version (for the time being).
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44187377/932dfbcc955515638e6b94be87a3d6ca2bfbb453.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44187377/8647dbcf566e3cb804bda420b69a63ecbe5af8ae.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44187377/a0647a99a8b083b513da88ce1ac023953fedeb4a.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44187377/ddefdcecaf2eaf75198eeb690273d3c8541d04c2.gif[/img]

I also designed some other things, like a custom font, logos, objects, items, furniture and a companion called V-Co9.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44187377/d1862a2a1f6da83cefe2cf2e0b2170e808588719.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44187377/e0d2e957f17482e68d1be05e78b26e5d89492a3a.gif[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44187377/e1d9de60880deb6c35492c36bcf0b7f0f714dd15.gif[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44187377/4c2222c91e4a296b641357accad43153eac29c4d.png[/img]
I'm currently working on the NPCs' individual hotel rooms. Everyone gets their own personal room. These are still unfurnished, but first the rough outline - then the details. I'm really enjoying designing the rooms.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44187377/9e7ef01d1ec71648954e85fe90d3247a9627103d.png[/img]

I've also already implemented the character creator in Godot and some important game mechanics such as the controls, scene changes, the dialogue system, tasks and some animations.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44187377/51bd785e75dd2748c4910da7f984ccc18c2c8bc2.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44187377/24c6ce46b17e1391fc1275ff41783acd9f64b84c.png[/img]
At this point I have to continue as quickly as possible so that it won't be long until a playable demo :)
I'm also working on promotional material such as flyers, business cards and T-shirts, as I want to present my game at conventions next year.

I hope you'll stay tuned and thank you for all the support and feedback I've received on the various platforms. I look forward to further progress and the next updates :)

Best regards,
pixlerin
